text: {"rules":[{"jurisdiction":"NJ","level":"state","category":"security_deposits","status":"in_force","title":"New Jersey Security Deposit Law: interest, notice and 30-day return","requirement":"Landlords must hold security deposits in an insured New Jersey bank or savings and loan in an interest-bearing account (or, for 10 or more units, an insured money market fund of a NJ-based investment company). The deposit may not be commingled with the landlord's property. Interest belongs to the tenant and is paid in cash or credited to rent annually. The landlord must give written notice of the bank, amount, account type and interest rate within 30 days of receipt and at each annual interest payment. After a tenancy ends, the landlord must return the deposit plus interest, less itemized deductions, within 30 days, by personal delivery or registered or certified mail. Deposits must be returned within 5 business days if the tenant is displaced by fire, flood, condemnation or evacuation. A new owner is responsible for the deposit and its interest. A tenant who does not receive proper notice or interest may apply the deposit plus 7% per annum interest to rent. A landlord who wrongfully withholds a deposit is liable for double the amount withheld plus costs and attorney's fees.","key_value":"Return within 30 days of tenancy termination; interest-bearing account;
